name: Happy to Wander
shortDescription: A Vancouver-based travel channel that walks first-time travellers through planning a trip step by step — flights, accommodation, documents and packing — mostly for Europe.
longDescription: The channel’s planning videos are built as chaptered walkthroughs: how to plan a Europe trip from the Schengen rules through flights, accommodation, getting around and packing; how to use Google Flights’ date grid and price history; how to travel cheaply; how to pack carry-on only. Around them sits a larger body of destination guides — 102 of the 167 long-form titles are framed for a named place or for “first timers” there — and packing videos, twelve of them sponsored by a merino clothing brand. 110 of the 167 long-form descriptions carry chapter markers, and most link a longer written guide on the presenter’s own site. Across the {{scannedWords}} most recent uploads the median runs {{medianPhrase}}.
notFor: Anyone planning long-term, multi-country or off-the-beaten-track travel — the planning advice is pitched at a first trip, largely to Europe — and anyone who wants booking advice kept apart from the booking services the presenter earns from.

categories.why: Teaches the planning sequence of a first trip in order — documents, flights, where to stay, getting around, packing — in chaptered videos a beginner can follow step by step, beside the category’s hour-long sessions on airfare and insurance.
categories.evidence: Of the 167 long-form uploads in a catalogue of 186, 29 pair a planning subject — booking flights or hotels, budgeting, itineraries, visas, packing — with a how-to or step-by-step framing: a step-by-step Europe trip plan, a Google Flights walkthrough, a guide to travelling cheaply, carry-on packing for first timers, and when to use third-party booking sites.

entryVideo.title: HOW TO PLAN A TRIP TO EUROPE (STEP BY STEP) FOR FIRST TIMERS | Flights, Accommodation & More!
entryVideo.whyThisOne: The whole planning sequence for a first trip in eighteen minutes — Schengen rules, how long to go, where to go, visas and documents, booking flights and accommodation, getting around and what to pack — the beginner level’s research, budget and pack-light steps in one pass.

caveats: The presenter earns from the booking choices the videos advise on: 145 of the 186 video descriptions carry an affiliate link to Booking.com, 132 a paid link to a travel-insurance provider, and 165 at least one commission-paying link to a transport, tour, car-hire or eSIM service. Separately, 44 of the 186 open with a placement marked as an ad — 26 an eSIM discount code, 12 a merino clothing brand’s sponsorship of the video, the rest luggage, electronics or a tour-booking site — and one eSIM set-up tutorial is sponsored by the eSIM provider it teaches. The entry video carries no ad placement; its description opens with a free planning workbook and puts the affiliate block below the chapters. The Europe focus means visa and entry rules are given for a Europe trip; check them for your own passport.

name: The White Coat Investor
shortDescription: A personal-finance channel for doctors and other high earners, run by a practising emergency physician, whose insurance teaching argues for buying cover against catastrophe and against mixing insurance with investing.
longDescription: The channel carries a weekly podcast, a shorter “Financial Boot Camp” series pitched as a first course in money, interview episodes with listeners who reached financial milestones, and a large number of short clips cut from them. Insurance is one recurring subject among investing, student loans and tax: whole life against term cover, what to do with a whole life or indexed universal life policy already bought, disability cover and its definitions, how much home and car insurance to carry, and employer health plans. The host’s stated position is that most working professionals need term life and disability cover and should keep insurance and investing apart. Everything is framed for physicians and similar high earners. {{shortCountWords|cap}} of the {{scannedWords}} most recent uploads run two minutes or less.
notFor: Anyone who wants examples at an ordinary income — the audience is doctors, and malpractice cover and own-occupation disability policies come up constantly — and anyone outside the US wanting product-level detail.
jurisdictionNote: US products and rules throughout — employer health plans, HSAs, state malpractice markets and US tax treatment of policy loans. The reasoning about when cover is worth buying, why term usually beats whole life, and what to check in a disability definition transfers; the products, prices and tax rules do not.

categories.why: Teaches insurance from the buyer’s side — cover for catastrophe first, and a sustained argument against products that bundle insurance with investment, which is the category’s advanced question.
categories.evidence: Across all 3,066 uploads, 44 of the 1,097 videos of eight minutes or more are titled on insurance: a 13-minute Boot Camp episode and a 45-minute podcast on whole life against term, a 51-minute episode on why mixing insurance and investing causes problems, how to surrender an indexed universal life policy, how much homeowners and car insurance to carry, own-occupation against any-occupation disability cover, and employer health plans compared.

entryVideo.title: Whole Life Insurance: What Doctors Need to Know - WCI Financial Boot Camp
entryVideo.whyThisOne: How whole life differs from term, what happens to the cash value, why the early returns disappoint, and the narrow cases where permanent cover makes sense — the beginner’s question of which policies you actually need, and the advanced one of when insurance and investing are bundled against you.

caveats: The channel takes sponsorship from an independent disability-insurance agent: 101 of the 3,066 video descriptions say so, from 2019 to this month, including 5 of the 44 insurance videos — a commercial interest in one of the decisions it advises on. Other episodes are sponsored by banks and student-loan lenders, and 1,462 descriptions link the channel’s own paid courses in a standing block. The entry video carries no sponsor or third-party placement. The advice is written for US physicians; check how it maps to your own income and country.

name: Jennifer May, Ph.D.
shortDescription: A licensed clinical psychologist and DBT programme coordinator teaching Dialectical Behaviour Therapy skills as short recorded lessons, one skill per video; the channel has not posted since February 2025.
longDescription: Jennifer May describes herself on the channel as a New York licensed clinical psychologist who has practised Dialectical Behaviour Therapy since 2001 and coordinates a DBT programme at a psychiatric centre. The catalogue is organised as courses rather than episodes: 89 of the 220 titles are DBT skills lessons, 33 are Radically Open DBT, and 37 belong to a series on sensorimotor psychotherapy. For boundaries, the relevant course is DBT’s interpersonal-effectiveness module, taught skill by skill — asking, refusing, keeping the relationship, keeping self-respect. Across the {{scannedWords}} most recent uploads the median runs {{medianPhrase}}.
notFor: Anyone who needs current or live material — the channel stopped posting in February 2025 — and anyone looking for treatment: these lessons explain DBT skills and are not a substitute for a DBT programme with a therapist.

categories.why: Teaches refusing and asking as short, separate DBT lessons of 11 to 22 minutes — the category’s beginner step of declining without over-explaining, in a length a first-timer will finish.
categories.evidence: 17 of the 218 videos of eight minutes or more across all 220 uploads are titled on boundaries, assertiveness, saying no or the interpersonal-effectiveness skills: the whole module as lessons of 11 to 22 minutes (its goals and obstacles, DEAR MAN, tips for asking assertively, GIVE, FAST, saying no, building and ending relationships, and a review of all of them), a 22-minute lesson on an expanded-DBT boundary skill, a 36-minute Radically Open DBT lesson on assertive asking, and two 47- and 55-minute lectures on boundary styles.

entryVideo.title: DBT - Interpersonal Effectiveness - Saying "No"
entryVideo.whyThisOne: Why saying no goes wrong — the automatic refusal and the fear of refusing — and the skills for moving to a considered no, in sixteen minutes: the beginner level’s practice of declining small things without over-explaining.

caveats: The channel has not posted since February 2025, and its boundary lessons date from 2020 to 2023. The lessons teach skills from a therapy normally delivered in a structured programme; they explain it rather than deliver it. None of the 220 video descriptions carries a sponsor, affiliate link or paid product.

name: Skye Wealth
shortDescription: An Australian personal-insurance advice firm whose advisers explain how life, TPD, trauma and income-protection policies behave at claim time, in long conversational episodes and many short clips.
longDescription: Skye Wealth describes itself as an insurance advice business operating under an Australian financial services licence, and its long-form videos are its advisers working through how cover actually behaves: what starts and resets an income-protection waiting period, benefit periods after a second claim, own- against any-occupation TPD definitions, underwriting loadings and declines, pre-existing conditions, and whether to hold cover inside or outside superannuation. Many are built around a claim scenario, and a weekly “This Week at Skye” episode covers regulator actions and industry news. Most uploads are short clips: {{shortCountWords}} of the {{scannedWords}} most recent run two minutes or less.
notFor: Anyone outside Australia — the products, super rules and regulators are Australian throughout — and anyone who wants insurance explained by someone who does not also arrange it for a living.
jurisdictionNote: Australian products and law throughout — insurance inside superannuation, the 2020 income-protection reforms, APRA, ASIC and AFCA. The questions to ask of a definition, a waiting period or a benefit period transfer to any market; the products, tax treatment and super rules do not.

categories.why: Explains how a policy behaves at claim time — definitions, waiting and benefit periods, underwriting — which is the category’s intermediate step of comparing cover on exclusions and claim behaviour rather than premium.
categories.evidence: Across all 1,721 uploads, 109 of the 188 videos of eight minutes or more are titled on insurance, running 13 to 49 minutes: TPD definitions and why claims are denied, income-protection waiting periods and benefit periods, underwriting loadings and declines, pre-existing conditions, cover inside against outside super, trauma against private health cover, and a 49-minute episode on whether adviser commissions inflate premiums.

entryVideo.title: Why TPD Gets Denied: The Definitions No One Explains
entryVideo.whyThisOne: Own occupation, any occupation, home duties and daily-living definitions of total and permanent disability, and how the one that applies can shift between applying and claiming — reading a policy for claim behaviour rather than price.

caveats: Skye Wealth is an insurance advice firm: it earns when a viewer arranges cover through it, which is a commercial interest in the decisions the videos discuss. The descriptions rarely sell directly — 5 of the 188 long-form descriptions invite the viewer to book a consultation with the firm — and the entry video’s carries no offer or link. No third-party sponsor or affiliate placement was found in the long-form descriptions. Everything is Australian; check how it maps to your own country.

name: Dave Lowell, CFP®
shortDescription: A Certified Financial Planner explaining personal-finance mechanics — mortgages, credit scores, interest rates, debt payoff, tax — in short sequenced lessons of eight to fifteen minutes.
longDescription: Dave Lowell describes himself on the channel as a Certified Financial Planner who has worked with clients from new graduates to the very wealthy. The channel began in April 2026, and its long-form catalogue — 89 videos, all posted between April and July 2026 — is built as short sequenced lessons: one on how mortgages work leads into one on rates, closing costs and amortization, then one on paying off the mortgage against investing. Credit and borrowing sit beside tax, estate planning, investing and real estate. Since August the channel has posted short clips: {{shortCountWords}} of the {{scannedWords}} most recent uploads run two minutes or less.
notFor: Anyone outside the US — the mortgages, PMI, credit bureaus and scores described are American — and anyone repairing damaged credit, which no lesson title covers.
jurisdictionNote: US lending throughout — FICO scores, the three US credit bureaus, PMI, escrow, 15- and 30-year fixed mortgages. How lenders price risk, how amortization front-loads interest and how to read the total cost of a loan transfer anywhere; the products, scores and consumer rights do not.

categories.why: Takes a borrower from how a score is built to how a mortgage is priced and amortized, in lessons short enough to follow in order — the category’s intermediate step of comparing loan structures rather than monthly payments.
categories.evidence: Across all 253 uploads, 14 of the 89 videos of eight minutes or more are titled on credit, loans, mortgages or debt, running 8 to 15 minutes: credit reports and scores, how lenders set interest rates from risk and debt-to-income, how mortgages work, rates, closing costs and amortization, HELOCs, paying off a mortgage against investing, and the order to pay debts off in.

entryVideo.title: Understanding Mortgage Rates, Closing Costs, and Amortization Explained
entryVideo.whyThisOne: Fixed against variable rates, what closing costs and PMI add, how to read an amortization table and why early payments are mostly interest, and 15 against 30 years, worked on a live example — comparing a loan’s structure and total cost rather than its monthly payment.

caveats: A young channel: it began in April 2026, and its long-form lessons were all posted between April and July 2026; since August it has posted short clips only. Descriptions carry almost no outside links — 3 of the 89 long-form descriptions link anywhere off YouTube — and no sponsor, affiliate or product placement was found in them.
